extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners and Central Reexamination Unit staff; patent owners and third‑party requesters and their practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, granting, denying, processing, and litigating decisions and procedural steps in inter partes reexamination proceedings (including standards for instituting reexamination, required content of decisions, forms, petitions, and submissions after an order).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for instituting reexamination (SNQ versus RLP)
rubrics_metrics.description: For requests filed prior to September 16, 2011, institution is based on whether a 'substantial new question of patentability' (SNQ) is raised; for requests filed beginning September 16, 2011 and ending September 15, 2012, institution is based on whether there is a 'reasonable likelihood that the requester will prevail' (RLP) with respect to at least one challenged claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner must identify at least one SNQ/RLP and explain how the cited prior art (patents and/or printed publications) establish that SNQ/RLP. The determination is made on the claims in effect at the time of determination (37 CFR 1.923). The examiner's substantive decision to institute is not subject to petition or judicial review except in very limited 'ultra vires' circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art considered for institution
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination whether an SNQ/RLP exists can be based upon any prior art patents or printed publications, not limited to the references relied upon in the request (35 U.S.C. 312(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If it is not clear a patent/printed publication predates the patent claims, the examiner must discuss why the reference is deemed available as prior art. References relied upon by the examiner should be cited on PTO‑892 unless already listed on equivalent requester forms (PTO/SB/08A/08B/42). Only supply copies of references where not already supplied to the patent owner and requester.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impermissible grounds for reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments based on grounds other than patents or printed publications (e.g., public use or on sale under 35 U.S.C. 102(b), abandonment under 35 U.S.C. 102(c)) are improper for reexamination and are not considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should note such improper grounds and not comment on them. See 37 CFR 1.906(c) and related MPEP cross‑references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content of decision granting reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision granting reexamination must (A) identify all claims and issues to be reexamined, (B) identify the patents and/or printed publications relied upon, and (C) provide a brief statement of the rationale supporting each SNQ/RLP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision should identify at least one SNQ/RLP and explain how the prior art establishes it; in a simple case adoption of the requester’s reasons may suffice. Use form PTOL‑2063 as cover sheet; include Form Paragraph 26.01 at the beginning of the decision and Form Paragraph 26.73 at the end when appropriate. Transmittal form PTOL‑2070 is used to forward Office actions and mailing copies to the third party requester.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content of decision denying reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision denying reexamination must state that no SNQ/RLP has been found and indicate, for each patent or publication cited in the request, why a SNQ/RLP has not been established by that citation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Form Paragraph 26.02 as the introductory paragraph in a decision denying reexamination. The examiner should respond to the substance of each argument raised by the third party requester that is based on patents or printed publications, and note but not analyze improper non‑patent grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel review and signatures for decision preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparation of the decision (grant or denial) involves setting up a panel review conference per MPEP § 2671.03; if the conference confirms the examiner’s preliminary decision, the decision is completed and signed by the examiner and initialed by two or more conferees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner may prepare the decision and any accompanying first Office action either before or after the conference and revise as needed. A PTOL‑2070 transmittal form with the third party requester’s address should be completed for mailing copies when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of forms and mailing/correspondence procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific PTO forms and procedures must be used for citing references and mailing decisions and Office actions (e.g., PTOL‑2063, PTOL‑2064, PTOL‑2070, PTO‑892, PTO/SB/08A/08B/42).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correspondence may be submitted via EFS‑Web (registered users) or by mail, fax, or hand to CRU addresses. For EFS‑Web transmissions, timely filing requires compliance with 37 CFR 1.6(a)(4) and inclusion of a certificate of transmission stating the date prior to expiration of the period. PTOL‑2070 removes need to retype requester address for mailings; attach a copy of the form to each Office action mailed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing rules and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) are not permitted in inter partes reexamination proceedings because 37 CFR 1.136 applies to 'an applicant' and not to a patent owner in reexamination; inter partes reexamination proceedings are conducted 'with special dispatch' per 35 U.S.C. 314(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owner extensions of time in inter partes reexamination are provided for in 37 CFR 1.956. Extensions of time are not available for third party requester comments, because statute fixes a 30‑day comment period from service of patent owner’s response (35 U.S.C. 314(b)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of prior art submitted after an order (post‑order submissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any prior art citations submitted under 37 CFR 1.501 after the date of the decision ordering inter partes reexamination are stored until the reexamination is concluded and will not be considered by the examiner during that reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After conclusion of the reexamination proceeding the submission is entered in the patent file. Note 37 CFR 1.902 governs such submissions by patent owners and third party requesters, and written statements under 37 CFR 1.501 are not permitted in inter partes reexamination (see MPEP § 2602).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑reviewability of institution determination (limits on petitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: A substantive determination by the Director to institute reexamination based on prior art patents or printed publications is not subject to review by petition or otherwise (per case law and statute).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions to vacate a reexamination order are extremely limited and will be granted only where the Office acted in 'brazen defiance' of its statutory authority (ultra vires). Where the examiner determines a reference is early enough to be prior art or is a printed publication, those determinations are not petitionable to vacate the order granting reexamination (35 U.S.C. 312(c) and precedent cited).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds permitting petition to vacate an order (37 CFR 1.181(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.181(a)(3) to vacate a reexamination order may be filed only in 'appropriate circumstances', for example where (A) the reexamination order is facially not based on prior art patents or printed publications; (B) reexamination is prohibited under 37 CFR 1.907; (C) all claims were held invalid by final federal court decision after appeals; (D) reexamination was ordered for the wrong patent; or (E) reexamination was ordered based on a duplicate copy of the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such petitions are to be rare, are delegated to the Director of the CRU, and the filing is limited to a single submission even if an opposition is filed by the third party requester. If filed, the third party may file a single opposition within two weeks of service to ensure consideration; electronic filing of oppositions is advisable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to review denial of reexamination (37 CFR 1.927 / 1.181)
rubrics_metrics.description: A third party requester may seek review of an examiner’s refusal to order inter partes reexamination by petition to the Director under 37 CFR 1.181 within one month of the mailing date of the denial (37 CFR 1.927).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a petition is filed the CRU Director reviews de novo. Decisions on such petitions are final and nonappealable; if no petition is filed within one month the denial becomes final and a partial refund of the filing fee is processed (35 U.S.C. 312(c), 37 CFR 1.26(c)). If the petition is granted the decision should state that an Office action will be mailed and the proceeding may be reassigned to another examiner (general rule: reassign where prior denial occurred). Time extension requests to file such petitions require a 37 CFR 1.183 petition with fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reassignment and examiner selection rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If an order for inter partes reexamination resulted from a petition under § 1.927, the reexamination will ordinarily be conducted by an examiner other than the examiner responsible for the initial determination under § 1.923; generally, reexamination proceedings are not reassigned to examiners involved in the original examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CRU Director can reassign to an original examiner only in unusual circumstances (e.g., no other examiner available with adequate knowledge). Where the examiner’s determination failed to find any SNQ/RLP, reassignment to another examiner is the general rule, unless exceptional circumstances justify otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision language and example usage (form paragraphs and sample decisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific sample language and form paragraphs are provided for decisions granting (¶ 26.01) and denying (¶ 26.02) inter partes reexamination, including tailored language for SNQ vs RLP timeframes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should use provided sample text as appropriate (e.g., 'A substantial new question of patentability affecting claim [1] ... is raised' or 'The present request ... establishes a reasonable likelihood that requester will prevail with respect to claim [1]'). Examples illustrate how to explain why particular references do or do not raise SNQs/RLPs and which claims will be reexamined.
